incidents.body:
Processing Delays and Intermittent Timeouts for Magic Containers

On June 1, Magic Containers experienced degraded service for approximately one hour due to a network connectivity issue in our hosting provider's environment. Customers running workloads may have seen increased processing delays, intermittent timeouts, temporary disruption, or reduced availability as some workloads were automatically rescheduled. The issue was resolved after the underlying network conditions stabilized, allowing scheduling activity to resume normally.

We are improving the resilience of Magic Containers so degraded connectivity can be detected and handled more effectively, not only complete outages. We are also adding safeguards to reduce unnecessary or duplicate workload rescheduling during degraded conditions, helping limit customer impact if similar infrastructure issues occur again.

incidents.body:
An internal process failure related to the management of our bunny.net domain with one of our domain registrars led to the temporary suspension of the domain, causing multiple services under bunny.net to become unavailable.

After identifying and confirming the issue, we worked with the registrar to restore the domain and all affected services are now recovering as DNS changes propagate globally. We have identified the root cause internally and are implementing additional safeguards and escalation procedures to ensure this cannot happen again.

During the outage, products and services under bunny.net experienced varying levels of disruption depending on DNS propagation and their dependency on bunny.net infrastructure and Bunny DNS.

Services including the Website, Dashboard, API, DNS, and related tools experienced widespread availability issues. Other products such as Stream and Magic Containers saw limited disruption and remained largely operational for most users, though some functionality was impacted depending on DNS resolution and service dependencies. Core services such as CDN delivery and Storage remained operational throughout the incident.

We will publish a full public RCA once the incident is fully resolved, including additional details around the timeline, service impact, root cause, and the preventative measures being implemented.

We're deeply sorry for the disruption and inconvenience caused. We expect the situation to fully resolve over the next few hours as DNS propagation completes worldwide. If you have any questions, please contact support@bunny.net.

incidents.body:
Migration to our new Logging Platform is now complete, and near real-time logs should be visible again.

Unfortunately, we had to accelerate the migration timeline as our legacy platform began struggling much sooner than expected. Because of this, we made the difficult decision to complete the migration before fully backfilling the expected 3 days of retained logging history.

At the moment, approximately 1.5 days of logs are available on the new platform. This will gradually increase and return to the full 3-day retention by Friday.

The raw, unprocessed logs remain stored on the legacy logging platform. If you require access to these logs and have a valid justification, please submit a support ticket, and we will do our best to recover them on a case-by-case basis.
